FIELD GUIDE · 01

THE BASE ARCHITECTURE

How a voice agent
hears, thinks, and speaks.

A voice agent is a conversation loop with six jobs. It captures sound, detects turns, understands meaning, makes a decision, uses tools, and returns speech.

00

THE SIMPLE MODEL

ears brain voice

Everything else improves speed, memory, control, or reliability.

01 / SYSTEM LOOP

One conversation.
Six connected stages.

Select a stage to inspect its responsibility. Each stage must have a clear input and output. This separation makes the system easier to test.

PLAYBACK RETURNS TO THE USER ↩

01 · CAPTURE

Turn air pressure into a clean audio stream.

The microphone and transport layer collect the user’s voice. The client normalizes the audio and sends small frames to the agent.

RECEIVES
Microphone signal
EMITS
Audio frames
WATCH FOR
Noise, echo, permissions

02 / TWO PATTERNS

Choose how audio
moves through the system.

Both patterns use the same conversation loop. They place the language boundary in a different location.

AUDIO IN Speech-to-text Audio becomes words
→
TEXT Language model Words become a decision
→
AUDIO OUT Text-to-speech Response becomes sound

BEST WHEN

You want clear transcripts, easy debugging, and the option to replace each provider.

TRADE-OFF

Three model calls can add latency. Emotion and timing can be lost at the text boundary.

GOOD FIRST BUILD

Yes. Each step is visible, testable, and easy to understand.

AUDIO IN Live session Continuous audio stream
→
NATIVE AUDIO MODEL Listen + reason + speak One model preserves tone, timing, and interruption context
→
AUDIO OUT Playback Streamed response

BEST WHEN

You need natural timing, low delay, and support for user interruption.

TRADE-OFF

The internal steps are less visible. Provider behavior can be harder to isolate.

GOOD FIRST BUILD

Yes, when a managed Live API handles the audio session for you.

A USEFUL RULE

Keep conversation behavior in the prompt. Keep permissions and business rules in code.

The model can propose an action. Your application must decide whether that action is allowed.

04 / ONE TURN

What happens after you speak.

  1. 01

    Listen

    Stream microphone frames.

  2. 02

    Close the turn

    Detect a pause or button release.

  3. 03

    Interpret

    Build meaning from audio or text.

  4. 04

    Resolve

    Answer directly or call a tool.

  5. 05

    Respond

    Stream speech as soon as possible.

↯

BARGE-IN IS A PARALLEL CONTROL LOOP

While the agent speaks, the input system still listens. New user speech stops playback, cancels generation, and starts the next turn.

05 / YOUR FIRST BUILD

Build the smallest loop that can hold a conversation.

Do not optimize the first version. Make every boundary visible. Log the transcript, model response, tool result, and playback state.

  1. 01

    Start with push-to-talk

    A button gives you reliable turn boundaries.

  2. 02

    Add one agent model

    Use one prompt and keep the task narrow.

  3. 03

    Return one spoken answer

    Stream it when possible. A complete response is fine first.

  4. 04

    Add one read-only tool

    Use a safe tool such as time, weather, or a local lookup.
